Plateau United technical adviser Gbenga Ogunbote has warned his players against complacency after their 3-0 victory over Kun Khalifat ended a four-match winless run in the Nigeria Premier Football League. The Peace Boys returned to winning ways on Tuesday at the New Jos Stadium, with Ogunbote expressing satisfaction with the response of his players following their recent struggles. “It was a good comeback for us after four games without a win. We needed a lot to psych the players up. Thank God we had one of the best moments, coming back to start winning. We hope and pray that we will be able to manage it,” Ogunbote told the media. The coach, however, insisted that his side must build on the victory rather than allow the result to make them complacent. “We will leverage on it. We will not relax like we had before. We had a slip; I did say before that it was a temporary setback,” he added. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The result ended a difficult spell for the Jos-based side and lifted them to eighth position on the league table. Ogunbote also expressed concern about officiating in away matches, saying he hoped his team would receive the same standard of refereeing on the road. “We still hope and pray that we will have the type of officiating that we get here in our away games. I can tell that we will go out and play very well,” he said. Plateau United will now seek to maintain their momentum when they face Ranchers Bees in their next league fixture.
